packageRules.description: Cargo crates are pinned deliberately and the committed Cargo.lock is the source of truth: a manifest-only bump desyncs the lock and fails resolution in every cargo-touching lane at once (reqwest 0.12 → 0.13 failed Format, Lint, Type-Check, Build, Unit, Desktop and both container builds together). Cargo upgrades are their own reviewed change.
The rust toolchain pin (mise) gates every lane at once under a compiler the repository has not shipped with; upgrades are their own reviewed change, not a grouped bump.

The rust builder and python runtime images compile and run the product under pinned toolchains; image jumps (rust 1.88 → 1.98, python 3.11 → 3.14) are their own reviewed change, not a grouped bump. Renovate split the retired `docker` manager into `dockerfile` and `docker-compose`.
The vendored third_party tree is pinned by name to the upstream revision it copies; its manifests must not move independently.

Every @adea-ai/* package rides one branch: the shared design system moves as a unit and the version pins are updated in place. The full validation suite — including the M7 capture-and-audit lane — runs when a human marks the draft ready; a held PR is a finding for the theme migration, not a chore.

Non-major external dependency updates ride one grouped draft branch per cycle. No auto-merge: GitHub refuses to attach it to a draft PR, and every PR must open as a draft because the code-foundry gates only run on the ready-for-review transition.

Pinned GitHub action SHAs are audited supply-chain controls (scripts/desktop-cache.test.mjs enforces the install-action pin); a digest bump is its own reviewed change, so it must not ride the external non-major group. Placed after the group rule so the null groupName clears it.
Major external bumps share one draft PR per cycle instead of one per package — a grouped major PR reads as one upgrade decision.
Code Foundry runtime pins are sync-managed (runtime_ref in code-foundry.yml) and must not be independently upgraded; a bump branched before a sync can resurrect legacy caller files when merged.
TypeScript stays on the 6.x line this repository pins; 7.x is a deliberate upgrade, not a routine bump.
